speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose the cause of your persistent bleeding and easy bruising, can you tell me if you have ever experienced bleeding after other surgeries or dental work? Additionally, have you noticed any blood in your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has the patient ever experienced prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, or has he had any episodes of heavy nosebleeds that were difficult to stop?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of joint swelling and easy bruising strongly suggests a coagulation factor deficiency like Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, PTT, Fibrinogen) and Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with a normal PT points towards an intrinsic pathway defect, likely Hemophilia A or B. I need to distinguish between the two specific factor deficiencies. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII level and Factor IX level.

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal Factor VIII and IX levels rule out Hemophilia A and B, which is unexpected given the prolonged PTT and family history. I need to check for other coagulation factor deficiencies or inhibitors that could explain these results. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI level and Lupus Anticoagulant screen.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor XI and Lupus Anticoagulant results, I am now considering von Willebrand Disease, which can sometimes present with a mildly prolonged PTT and normal standard factor assays if not specifically tested. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal vWF studies effectively rule out von Willebrand Disease, yet the isolated prolonged PTT persists. I must now evaluate for a deficiency in contact activation factors, specifically Factor XII, or investigate the presence of a specific inhibitor like anti-Factor VIII antibodies that might not have been detected yet. REQUEST TEST: Factor XII level and Bethesda Assay for Factor VIII inhibitors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Factor XII level rules out Factor XII deficiency, and the negative Bethesda assay excludes acquired hemophilia. Given the family history of hemarthrosis (joint swelling) and easy bruising, this clinical picture remains highly suggestive of Hemophilia A or B despite the previously reported normal factor levels, which may have been erroneous or misinterpreted. I will request a repeat confirmation of Factor VIII and IX levels along with a mixing study to check for time-dependent inhibitors. REQUEST TEST: Repeat Factor VIII and IX levels with Mixing Study.

speaker: Doctor
text: The persistent normal results for Factor VIII and IX despite a prolonged PTT and strong clinical suspicion of hemophilia suggest a potential laboratory error or a rare variant. speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the confusing laboratory results showing normal factor levels, the clinical presentation of a male patient with a family history of joint swelling and bleeding, combined with an isolated prolonged PTT, is classic for Hemophilia A.
